name: Apollo 11
summary: First crewed landing on the Moon. Descent stage and instruments remain on the surface.
key_discoveries: Confirmed the lunar surface could support a spacecraft
Laser reflector still used today to measure Earth-Moon distance
why_it_matters: The descent stage and retroreflector remain on the Moon. The reflector is still used by scientists to measure the distance between Earth and the Moon with high precision.
story: On 20 July 1969 the Lunar Module Eagle landed in the Sea of Tranquility. After the moonwalk, the ascent stage lifted off, leaving the descent stage and scientific instruments on the surface. Those pieces of hardware are still there.

images.alt: Astronaut Buzz Aldrin on the lunar surface with Neil Armstrong reflected in his visor

name: Viking 1 Lander
summary: First U.S. lander to operate successfully on Mars. Worked for more than six years.
key_discoveries: First detailed surface images of Mars
why_it_matters: Viking 1 proved soft landings on Mars were possible and delivered the first long-term scientific data from the Martian surface. Later missions built on its lessons.
story: Viking 1 landed on Mars in July 1976. Designed for 90 days, it operated for more than six years. It sent the first high-resolution images of the Martian surface and ran biology experiments. Contact was lost in 1982. The lander remains on the surface.

images.alt: First clear image from the surface of Mars by Viking 1
